newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police charge sect members - reports.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police charge sect members - reports.

text.p: Belgian police on Thursday detained and charged two leading members of a religious sect after raids the day before on up to seven houses in western Belgium, radio and television reports said.
The men, named as Andre Pestiaux and Dominique Le Maire, were charged with fraud, holding people against their will and association with criminals.
Pestiaux, head of the Cor Unum (Single Heart) sect, was also charged with illegally practising medicine.
The 45-year-old, dubbed Father Andre de St Paul and the "13th Apostle" by his followers, was reported to have formed the sect after saying he had seen Christ every day during a spell in 1984.
The sect practised what Belgian news agency Belga called natural medicine. It rejected vaccinations, blood transfusions and surgery.
Under Belgian law preventative vaccination against a number of childhood diseases is mandatory.
The sect's bookkeeper, Marie-Louise Boutiau, was charged with fraud and criminal association but not detained.
The charges were brought by the public prosecutor in the town of Tournai. On Wednesday, the prosecutor led searches in houses in Leuze-en-Hainaut and Bon-Secours on the border with France.
The raids were prompted by complaints from neighbours.
Police had wanted to check that Cor Unum followers, who lived off gifts of money and goods, were not being held against their will or suffering ill-treatment.

Behind one house was a large bricked-over yard with a cross and altar. Belgian television said there had been religious gatherings of up to 200 people there, with some coming from Austria, Germany and France.
